citation.title: Kinetic profile inference with outlier detection using support vector machine regression and Gaussian process regression
citation.authors: Kim M., Ko W.H., Kwak S., Joung S., Lee W., Kim B., Kim D., Lee J.H., Sung C., Na Y.-S., Ghim Y.-C.
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/1741-4326/ad7304 (this paper's own DOI, PDF p2 header)

scope_read.limitations: Figures were read from rendered pages. The paper does not state the CES impurity species. It gives no runtime numbers.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The GP is a spatial profile regression at a single time slice, not a temporal model.
claim_checks.source_finding: The GP is defined over measurement positions in major radius R. It uses a Gibbs kernel with core/edge length scales and pedestal location/width, plus gradient constraints at the axis and wall. Each profile is fitted at one time slice. Hyper-parameters are handled by MAP or by NUTS marginalization.
claim_checks.locator: p6 Sec 3.1 Eqs 15-19; p8 Sec 3.3 Eq 25; pp8-10 Sec 4, Figs 6-8
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: GP regression has been applied to KSTAR CES ion-temperature data as a spatial profile fit at individual time slices, with an SVMR screen to remove outliers before fitting [Kim2024].
claim_checks.qualification: This describes this paper only. Do not generalize it to all prior GP work.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: KSTAR CES reports contain occasional abrupt outliers caused by spectral-fit failures.
claim_checks.source_finding: Outliers were labelled by hand as abrupt changes in both space and time, using profiles at t0±10 ms. The authors report that such points tend to coincide with poor fits. One shown case is a Levenberg-Marquardt Gaussian fit failure. The authors describe outliers as quite low in number but give no rate. The 120-profile dataset was deliberately balanced, with 60 profiles containing outliers.
claim_checks.locator: p3 Sec 1; p5 Sec 2.2; pp11-12 App A, Figs A1-A2
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Reported CES temperatures are fitted products, and isolated fit failures can produce abrupt outliers in the reported values [Kim2024].
claim_checks.qualification: The causal link rests on a tendency plus one illustrated case. Labelling was subjective and used future frames. No frequency can be cited.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The method is real-time or causal.
claim_checks.source_finding: The motivation is automated outlier removal for large offline profile datasets, for example as neural-network training data. MAP is described only qualitatively as fast. No timing or deployment is reported.
claim_checks.qualification: Do not cite this paper for latency or online use.

input_target_timing.inputs: CES-reported Ti values and their uncertainties at multiple R positions in one time slice, plus imposed gradient priors
input_target_timing.outputs: Posterior Ti(R) profile and gradient; per-point outlier flags
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Offline, spatial, within a single frame. Outlier labelling used neighbouring past and future frames.
input_target_timing.source_diagnostic_as_input: Yes. The CES reports are both the input and the fitted quantity.
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: The paper works with reported Ti. There is no independent truth, and outlier labels involve subjective judgement (App A).

validation.split_unit: Profiles: 120 from 2017-2022, randomly split 84/36 (7:3). Test F1 0.857, precision 0.783, recall 0.947 (p5 Sec 2.3; p6 Table 2).
validation.temporal_order: Not preserved; the split was random across campaigns.
validation.unknowns: Whether frames from the same shot appear in both training and test sets. Population outlier rate. Performance on a single chord or a single campaign.

forbidden_inferences: Transferring the SVMR F1 to our chord or to 2022 data
Treating CES Ti as physical truth
Assuming the impurity is carbon based on this paper
Treating this GP as a causal nowcaster
Claiming all KSTAR GP work is spatial
Claiming the CES routine is now fixed (authors say only that it is being improved)
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. It is an offline spatial cleaner and profile fitter. It could motivate robustness of the reported label in our setting. It is not a comparator for causal temporal nowcasting, and it does not show that hold or causal-GP baselines fail.
